Content.description: Run a script to find specific processes running in EC2 instances.

windowsProcessNames.description: Specify the process names (comma-separated) to be searched on the instance.

linuxProcessNames.description: Specify the process names (comma-separated) to be searched on the instance.

runCommand:
IFS="," read -ra process_keywords <<< "{{ linuxProcessNames }}"

instanceId=`curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id`
filepath="/var/lib/amazon/ssm/$instanceId/inventory/custom/Processes.json"
[[ -f ${filepath} ]] || touch $filepath

declare -a results
for process_keyword in "${process_keywords[@]}"; do
  echo "Checking ${process_keyword}"
  if [[ $(ps -A -o cmd --no-headers | grep -i "${process_keyword}" | grep -v grep -c) -ge 1 ]]; then
    [[ "${results[@]}" =~ "${process_keyword}" ]] || results+=("$process_keyword")
  fi

  # Approach 2: log the entire process string
  # ret=$(ps -A -o cmd --no-headers | grep ${process_keyword} | grep -v 'grep' | awk -vORS=, '{print $0}')
  # IFS=","
  # for p in ${ret}; do
  #   [[ "${results[@]}" =~ ${p} ]] || results+=($p)
  # done
done

# Write to file
cat > ${filepath} << EOF
{
  "SchemaVersion": "1.0",
  "TypeName": "Custom:Processes",
  "Content": [
EOF
for p in "${results[@]}"; do
  cat >> ${filepath} << EOF
      {"ProcessName": "${p}"},
EOF
done
# Replace the last comma (if exists)
sed -i '$s/,$//' ${filepath}
cat >> ${filepath} << EOF
  ]
}
EOF
# Dump the file for debugging
cat ${filepath}
